News.title: Lawyer slams Ryanair crew who ‘didn’t offer man water’ after his head was sucked out plane’s window
News.content:
RYANAIR crew members did not even offer a man water after he was sucked through a shattered cabin window at 20,000ft, the victim’s lawyer claimed.

Ljubiša Karović‘s head and arm were left dangling out of the stricken jet and exposed to freezing 370mph winds for several minutes.



His heroic wife, Svetlana, clung on to the 61-year-old for dear life as he passed in and out of consciousness, saying that she thought at the time: “If we die, we die together”.

Another brave bystander helped tug Ljubiša back through the smashed window before he could be pulled from the plane.



In the aftermath, terrified passengers attempted to plug the gaping hole with a piece of luggage, but it was swiftly sucked from the plane.

A sturdier suitcase eventually did the trick.



But Ljubiša was left badly hurt with friction burns and serious injuries all over his body.

Despite pleas from Svetlana and other passengers, crew members are said to have denied repeated requests to bring him water and did nothing to help.



Businessman Ljubiša remains in hospital, where he is recovering from his wounds and a severe case of shock.

The Serbian couple’s lawyer, Vasilis Tsiaras, slammed the airline for failing to reach out to their shaken clients.

He told The Sun: “They didn’t say anything. They show no remorse.”



Ryanair did not provide a comment when approached by The Sun.

Svetlana praised the heroic intervention of a man and woman who helped hold on to her husband on last Friday’s flight from Thessaloniki, Greece to Memmingen, Germany.

She said: “That man helped me a lot. I would like to meet him, to thank him personally.”

Reliving the nightmare ordeal, Svetlana told Greek channel ERT: “I was scared that the plane would crash.

“My husband has serious injuries. He’s wearing a neck brace and at the very mention of planes he shakes.



“I’m also in a very bad psychological state and am taking sedatives. I was scared that people’s lives would be lost.”

Aside from the friction burns, the incident has left Ljubiša with psychological obstacles.

The 61-year-old sells and rents flats in the Greek resorts of Paralija and Olympic Beach, which means he needs to fly frequently for business.

But the experience has left him “extremely scared” of flying, said Vasilis.

Shocking footage showed the aftermath of the chaos – with oxygen masks seen hanging down and a gaping hole where one of the windows once was.



The plane was able to perform an emergency landing at Thessaloniki, where the pilot was left crying on the tarmac.

The doomed plane has been taken to a hangar at Thessaloniki airport for examination.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Aviation experts are now probing how a piece of the jet’s engine was able to dislodge and shatter the window.

Vasilis told BILD: “Ryanair’s claim that the window simply came loose is untrue. Experts have already determined that a broken engine part was hurled from the turbine against the cabin window and destroyed it.”

News.title: Vile trans troll who wished ‘extremely painful’ death on Ann Widdecombe is just tip of iceberg for nasty Green Party
News.content:
WHEN I first heard that Ann Widdecombe had died I found myself reacting like a human being.

I thought to myself, “Oh no, how sad, I hope her friends and family are coping.”





What I didn’t do was jump on social media to declare her death “good news”.

Neither did I then add how I hoped she died “an extremely painful death” and was “handcuffed to the bed as she screamed in agony”.

No, that was someone called Heather Herbert, a trans woman who works as a web developer at the University of Aberdeen.

Heartless Herbert made the comments on the BlueSky social media platform, shortly after Ann’s death was announced (and before it was declared a murder).

In case you’re not familiar with it, BlueSky is a sort of X for snowflake liberals who don’t like Elon Musk’s rowdy site because it’s full of people who, if they disagree with you, might say something like, I dunno, “I hope you die an extremely painful death”.

Well, horrid Heather didn’t care who his audience was and when taken to task over the disgraceful remarks just doubled down, sneering: “I’m done with being nice to pieces of human garbage like her.”

Gosh, what a valuable addition to the sisterhood this delightful doll is proving to be.

Police have since been investigating whether any of the comments constituted hate speech.





Initially they thought not (a sensible view, to be fair) but, intriguingly, have now launched “additional inquiries”.

Yet in a world bursting at the seams with excitable trolls craving attention, bile merchants like Heather Herbert dancing on the graves of those they disliked are no longer surprising.

Neither is something else about this charming individual. Four years ago the “trans activist” stood unsuccessfully in a by-election, hoping to become a councillor for the good folk of Aberdeen.

And the party he was representing?

You guessed it, the Greens.

Of course it was.

It’s becoming a new rule of thumb in politics that all the most abhorrent “activists” on the left will eventually be offered a home in the new Nasty Party.

The Greens have become the left-wing equivalent of Restore Britain, a home for extremists too bonkers for any mainstream party.

Mercifully, wise Aberdonians realised this was a bad idea and voted for someone else but Herbert remains a member of the Scottish Greens.



So the ragbag of a party has now been forced to look into the matter with a spokesperson sighing: “We are aware of the posts and have received complaints that are being investigated.”

Here we go again, another volley of grievances against one of its members.

One that comes just days after Zack Polanski’s England and Wales Greens were forced to admit that they are drowning in so many complaints they simply cannot cope.

According to The Times, in the year to June, 116 accusations were made against its members for wrongdoing.

Of those only 18 were concluded.

They include candidates suspended over antisemitic comments — 30 were accused at one point — and racial hatred.

Harry Clarke, the poor sod tasked with fielding all these complaints, told a meeting last month the procedures were “simply not fit for purpose”, adding: “We lack processes in almost every area of complaints and discipline.”

It’s no surprise that Wacko Zacko, who has laughably claimed his party have had only a “handful” of complaints, has completely failed to get a grip on this.

You could argue he’s been too busy embroiled in his own scandals, such as not paying council tax on his houseboat.

So busy is he that he couldn’t even find the time to vet his initial candidate for the recent Makerfield by-election, who pulled out hours after announcing he was standing when it emerged he’d described the firebombing of Jewish ambulances in North London as a “false flag”.



But I don’t think it’s the lack of time or internal “processes” that is the problem for Zack Polanski, it’s a deliberate lack of curiosity.

He knows that all these complaints are likely to be just the tip of the iceberg for the Greens, whose membership has ballooned by over 130,000 since September.

If he scratches too hard he will only confirm that his increasingly disturbing party is packed to the rafters with Heather Herberts.

BIN IT, BURN I WENT to the Silver Clef Awards last week, run by the heart-warming music therapy charity, Nordoff and Robbins, to squeeze cash out of rich people in the music biz. And squeeze they did, with attendees handing over £800,000 for tickets and auction swag. Andy Burnham was there as “guest of honour” of Mancunian indie luvvies James, to whom he presented the Legend award. Lapping up the moment on stage Our Andy – dressed in bomber jacket and Adidas trainers, natch – said, joshing: “I am not going to talk politics… except to say this: Count Binface, you are carrying the hopes of the nation.” LOL, what a card! But while his lefty larks might have appealed to the idealistic pop stars in the room, not everyone was pleased to see him. Like the millionaires who actually run the industry, terrified at how much this socialist is about to cost them. And who were no doubt thinking: “Oh sit down, oh sit down!”

Ali G can play his ace with Wimbo dullards

PO-FACED Wimbledon security gave Sacha Baron Cohen a dressing down at their annual jamboree after he turned up dressed as his idiotic alter ego, Ali G, clutching what looked like weed.

Of course, this most humourless of annual sporting events can’t possibly have anyone sending up all those celebrity liggers mainlining free Champagne. So will they now slap him with a lifetime ban like they gave a 19-year-old Piers Morgan after he snuck past security into the Royal Box?

If so, Sacha has an, ahem, ace up his sleeve to hit back with.

Just imagine all those toffs at the stuffy All England Tennis Club clutching their pearls as “Ali” rolls out his trademark inquiry: “Is it cos I is black?”

HAD BY BEEB EVERY damn time. Just when I think I’ve balanced my books perfectly so I can stagger to the next paycheck…BOOM, I’m suddenly £44.87 in the red. The culprit? The bloody TV licence, now a lumpy £180 a year. And again I wonder if I’m getting enough bang for my buck. My current BBC diet is Today, background noise from 6Music and World Cup games not on ITV. I rarely get control of the box as the family are bingeing Netflix. So I’m not surprised that another HALF A MILLION people ditched their licence last year. Why pay so much for something you don’t really use? Especially when it’s handed over to smarmy DJs that apparently can’t get by on less than £750,000 a year. The BBC keeps telling us it’s so skint it must sack people and ditch shows people like. Yet somehow it still finds the cash to pay stars (and execs) far more than they could make in the commercial sector. Ever get the feeling you’ve been had?

TIME TO ‘AIR AN EXCUSE

TERRIFYING words from the wife of Ljubisa Karovi, the man nearly sucked out of a window at 20,000 feet on a Ryanair flight.

“I reacted immediately and grabbed his legs. I thought, ‘If we die, we die together.’ It was horrible,” Svetlana Grkovic told us this week.



This should be terrible publicity for the cocky Ryanair, which likes nothing more than ridiculing the complaints of its customers on social media.

So I wait with bated breath to see what cynical stunt The World’s Greediest Airline comes up with after this PR disaster.

No doubt someone in marketing is working up a new charge they can foist on customers… for speedy exiting.

WHERE EAGLES SCARE AND there was me thinking the vegan crowd had got the message and piped the hell down. Oh no, they’re still active, this time pestering a bird of prey show in County Durham claiming falconry encourages “unnatural behaviours”. The Hopetown Darlington museum has been forced to scrap the event over fears of some kind of bad-tempered protest (and let’s face it, when the vegan nutters get going with their direct action they make the angriest of eagles look like a budgerigar). What a ridiculous world these vegans live in, one that now wants to deny people up-close encounters with some of Britain’s most majestic creatures. Does it not occur to them that when we humans have a more intimate relationship with our fauna we tend to be less inclined to want to stuff it in a sausage roll?

LIONEL RICHIE is to become the latest singer to be turned into a hologram “live artist”.

How long before we really will see him Dancing On The Ceiling?

News.title: Andy Burnham opens door to a wealth tax saying people would have to pay ‘a little more’
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has opened the door to a wealth tax – saying people would have to pay “a little more”.

The incoming PM said he would make “difficult” decisions that could see people charged on their assets.



A wealth tax has long been a hobby horse of left-wingers but many economists say it would actually cost money because rich people would leave the country.

Asked about the possibility of such a levy he told Gary Lineker’s podcast: “I’m not going to rule things out right now.



“I do believe we need a greater sense of fairness and people feeling that things are being done in the right way and a fair way.”

He added: “At some point that might be having to ask for a little more. But, you know, those decisions are not for now. They’re for another day.”

Mr Burnham has already committed to sticking to Labour’s manifesto not to raise the headline rates of income tax, national insurance or VAT.

A wealth tax comes in different variations but could see the rates of capital gains increased.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said: “Andy Burnham isn’t even Prime Minister yet but he’s already talking about raising your taxes again.

“We are heading for another summer of chaos with Labour obsessing about who they can tax to pay for more benefits.”



Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick, said: “Burnham has finally broken his two week silence and admitted that he will hike people’s taxes.

“But he won’t say which ones. He should stop hiding and rule out the ten taxes – £3,450 for every family – he’s previously supported but has no mandate for.

“Reform UK will fight him at every turn. We are the only party standing up for the hard working people that hold this country together.”

News.title: After Kemi twisted the knife, there were tears for Keir – but what about the tears for the country he’s betrayed?
News.content:
It was possible for a fleeting moment yesterday to watch Sir Keir Starmer’s final and finest performance and think, “We’re going to miss you.”

Gone was the peevish, puce-faced prima donna who has adorned the Treasury Despatch Box for two long and miserable years.



Here was the Prime Minister Sir Keir might have been. A fluent, mature statesman with a sense of humour in total command of a sympathetic House of Commons.

He set the scene with a warm tribute to Ann Widdecombe, expressing his “horror” at her brutal murder last week.



“Nobody had more political courage,” he said. Some of the more spiteful socialists sitting purse-lipped alongside might have shown similar grace.

Veteran blubber Rachel Reeves came close to tears at moments, probably knowing she’s on her way out too.

Watching from the public gallery, Sir Keir’s wife Lady Vic could feel proud of the man she has loved and supported through two torrid years as the most despised PM in history.

All that bitterness and grief was briefly suspended as friends, enemies and Labour MPs queued to praise the man they were about to bury.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch was in virtuoso form, promising to be kind for a change.

“I want to ensure I get the tone right,” she said, archly.



“So I looked back to his last questions to Boris Johnson. Luckily for him, I will be much more gentle than he was.”

She praised her antagonist for perhaps the only real success of the Starmer regime — his unstinting support for Ukraine in its war against Russia.

Then she unsheathed the stiletto.

“I remember when I started this job — he was very helpful to me, saying that I wouldn’t last the year. Life comes at you fast,” she beamed.



“He spent a long time laughing that I’d lost control of my party. I think he should have been paying attention to his backbenchers instead of mine.”

Sir Keir rose to the occasion yesterday with dignity, humour and, yes, some emotion as he listed poignant moments during his brief stint in Number Ten.

He recalled hugging Volodymyr Zelensky — the Ukrainian president’s “first human contact after being attacked” by Donald Trump in the Oval Office.

“It was a very emotional moment,” said Sir Keir, choking back a sob.



Even the PM’s murderous Cabinet seemed to melt.

It is amazing how brutal politicians will lay down their cut-throat razors when one of their “big beasts” is committing hara-kiri.

Especially in the case of Sir Keir, who after all, led Labour to a landslide — only to be crucified by his 402 MPs, not one of whom dared to challenge him openly.

The only politician with the nerve — or gall — to grab his crown slipped into the chamber for one last gloat while his elected leader was still alive and breathing. Andy Burnham, the long-lashed assassin, slid on to the government benches without saying a word. But his name was on everyone’s lips.

As was England striker Jude Bellingham’s ahead of England’s battle with Argentina.



Football is the Labour Party’s lingua franca. Arsenal fan Sir Keir said watching the big match on telly was one of his last prime ministerial duties.

“I don’t care what the score is — as long as we win,” he said to cheers from every party — except the SNP.

Veteran Tory MP Graham Stuart tied the two together with a deceptively vicious poke at Labour’s two-faced MPs.

“Politics, like football, is a ruthless game,” he said, “and he’s been handed a red card by the 400 dodgy referees behind him. What advice do you have for Andy Burnham to ensure that he doesn’t end up with an early bath?”

“Nothing I can say in public,” said Sir Keir with a tight smile.



So how is it ending for Sir Keir Starmer, the latest ex-Prime Minister, who promised to “bring about the change the country has decisively voted for”.

All political careers end in tears, they say. Those tears are being shed by the country Keir Starer deceived and betrayed.

That betrayal — on taxes, jobs for young people, the cost of living, law and order, two-tier justice and the relentless boatloads of mostly single young men — is all his as PM.

It is a shocking charge sheet.

Starmer has landed Britain on Benefits Street. He has reneged on his first duty to protect the nation.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has turbocharged our huge national debt. He has left us at the mercy of human rights judges and the unaccountable International Court of Justice. In one sense, he has delivered change as promised.

He just never told us in advance what that change would be or how dearly we, our children and our grandchildren would have to pay for it.

News.title: Mum who hid drugs in Kinder Egg capsule jailed for running cocaine and crack supply line from own home
News.content:
A MUM who hid drugs in a Kinder Egg capsule has been jailed for running a cocaine and crack supply line from her home.

Nicole Locke, 33, was identified by police investigating a phone number linked to the criminal trade.



Detectives raided her house last month.

South Wales Police said: “Officers found Locke in one of the bedrooms.



“When arrested her phone was seized and the number of the drug line was from Locke’s phone.

“Officers found a plastic bag containing white powder and £155 cash.

“Officers also searched Locke’s car where they found £180 cash.

“They also found one bag containing white powder.

“And a Kinder Egg containing white powder.”

Locke, of Tonypandy, Rhondda Cynon Taf, was jailed for five years and six months at Merthyr Tydfil crown court.



She admitted being concerned in the supply of cocaine and being concerned in the supply of crack cocaine.

The mum also pleaded guilty to acquiring/using criminal property.

News.title: Most Brits back drilling North Sea instead of relying on overseas gas imports, shows poll
News.content:
BRITS overwhelmingly back drilling the North Sea instead of relying on overseas gas imports, a poll shows.

Voters appear to have issued a rebuke to Ed Miliband’s ban on new oil and gas exploration licences.



YouGov research shows 58 per cent of the public say the priority should be using our own natural resources rather than taking supplies from abroad.

Just 11 per cent said the priority should be shoring up overseas imports, and 31 per cent were unsure.



While support for North Sea drilling is particularly strong among Tory and Reform voters, even Labour voters predominantly back using British oil and gas.

Energy Secretary Mr Miliband has been refusing to slow down his Net Zero drive despite calls to boost our energy security.

However there is speculation Andy Burnham could force him to drop the opposition to the Jackdaw and Rosebank oil and gas fields opening.

Mike Foster, chief executive of the Energy Utilities Alliance that commissioned the poll said: “The public understand something that too many politicians seem reluctant to say out loud: if Britain still needs gas, it makes no sense to import it from abroad when we have our own supplies in the North Sea.”

“This polling shows a clear common-sense majority in favour of home-grown energy over greater dependence on foreign imports.

“Voters want security, affordability and realism — not policies that simply offshore our energy needs, jobs and emissions.”



Tory leader Kemi Badenoch will today travel to Aberdeen to continue her campaign against Mr Miliband’s position.

The Scottish city is feeling the brunt of Labour’s Net Zero drive with unions warning thousands of jobs in the industry will be culled.

Ms Badenoch said: “We warned Ed Miliband that thousands of jobs in Aberdeen and across our country were at risk in the oil and gas industry, because he was putting ideology ahead of common sense. He refused to listen and blocked new North Sea licenses.



“Now that Miliband is vying to be Andy Burnham’s Chancellor, he’s apparently willing to change his tune and back drilling.”

News.title: Influencer, 30, dies on honeymoon after head-on crash with motorcycle while cycling through mountains
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

NEWLYWED TRAGEDY Influencer, 30, dies on honeymoon after head-on crash with motorcycle while cycling through mountains

A NEWLYWED outdoor influencer has died two weeks after a tragic crash with a former world ski champion on a motorbike left her in critical condition.

Laura Viktoria Härtig, 30, was cycling down a mountain road in northern Italy on her racing bike when she collided head-on with a motorcycle.



At the wheel was once-celebrated ski star Peter Runggaldier, 56, who had been coming round a bend when the fatal crash occurred.

The force of the impact split Laura’s bike in two.



Paramedics rushed to the scene where she was resuscitated and airlifted to a hospital in Bolzano, South Tyrol.

Runggaldier was also left seriously injured and airlifted to a hospital in Trento.

The ex-ski star won silver in the downhill event at the 1991 World Championships and followed it up with the Super-G World title four years later.

Doctors fought to save Laura’s life for 19 days and she had been transferred to a specialist clinic in her native Bavaria.



But she sadly succumbed to her injuries on Sunday.

The outdoor influencer had just tied the knot with her husband, Tillman, in the South Tyrol mountains just a few days earlier.

The newlyweds planned to spend their honeymoon in the mountains she loved so much.



Laura documented her mountain adventures and hikes with her 53,000 followers on Instagram.

Her final post shared photos of her dream wedding against a picturesque alpine backdrop, just two days before the accident.

Runggaldier has not publicly commented on the tragedy but has asked for understanding over his silence.

He is reportedly cooperating with police.

Prosecutors in Trento are now probing how the fatal accident occurred before they decide whether to file criminal charges.



Laura’s death is one of a string of cycling deaths on Italian roads this summer.

Cycling prodigy Samuele Privitera, 19, died after an accident during a pro race in Pontey, northwest Italy, on July 16.

The Sella Pass where Laura’s crash occurred is a popular road for mountain biking enthusiasts, but sees heavy traffic through the summer months.

News.title: Tragedy as mum & her two young children drown in Spain after swimming in popular dam lake
News.content:
SWIMMING TRAGEDY Tragedy as mum & her two young children drown in Spain after swimming in popular dam lake

A MUM and her two children have died in a horror triple drowning at a popular swim spot.

The woman, 29, and her kids aged 11 and three, were found dead in the Esca River in Spain.



The exact spot of the tragedy was the Roncal dam – a beloved picnicking spot with trees and clear blue waters at the heart of the Pyrenees.

Paramedics and an air ambulance raced to the dam after the alarm was raised at 4:39pm today.



They worked for over an hour to revive the family – but sadly all three were confirmed dead at the scene.

The Civil Guard are treating the deaths as accidental but have launched a probe to confirm there were no suspicious circumstances.

The identity of the mother and her children, from Roncal Valley, has not yet been made public.

Following the tragedy, Roncal City Council has declared three days of official mourning.



In a statement, they said: “Roncal Town Council wishes to express, on behalf of the entire town, its deep sorrow for the incident, its solidarity with the families and friends of the deceased, and its willingness to assist the affected families with any necessary procedures.”

It comes just one day after two identical twin boys were found dead in Catalonia.

The brothers, aged 11, had left home to play football – but when they did not return for dinner, their parents raised the alarm.

Two police forces mobilised in a major search party for the missing children.

Cops searched through the night and into the morning of July 14 when they made a tragic discovery.



The clothes of the twins were found on the bank of the river Ter at 11am, followed by the bodies of the twins, one at 1pm and the other at 2pm.

Police believe the brothers drowned after going into the river to cool off after their match.

The parents of the twins have been offered psychological support following their devastating loss.

And last month, the mum and grandmother of a five-year-old boy drowned after jumping into a river to save the child’s life.

The boy was paddleboarding near a dam on a family day out in a Spanish holiday hotspot when a powerful current began to sweep him away.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

His 32-year-old mum reportedly leapt into the water to try and rescue the boy, followed by his 52-year-old granny.

Fishermen later found the child clinging on to a tree trunk.

News.title: Tesco trials huge change to UK supermarkets as ‘6ft AI robot’ spotted in store
News.content:
Tesco trials huge change to UK supermarkets as ‘6ft AI robot’ spotted in store

A new life-sized robot is being trialed in Tesco to detect missing stock and pricing mistakes - and to save staff from having to carry out manual checks

View 2 Images The robots use AI to scan supermarket aisles (Image: Jam Press/Simbe)

Tesco is trialing a new 6.5ft aisle-roaming robot to help detect missing stock and pricing errors.

‌



The life-sized machine will use AI and computer vision to independently roam supermarket aisles and continuously monitor shelves - saving staff from having to carry out manual checks.

‌



Tesco said the Tally robot by Simbe Robotics will also help spot gaps on shelves so that staff can better boost visibility. According to Simbe, Tally can spot 10 times more out-of-stock products than those found in manual checks.

‌



The machine can also pick up on pricing errors and items displayed in the wrong location, then send over reports to store colleagues so that the issues can be quickly resolved.

Posting an image of the bot at a Tesco store, one Reddit user said: "Walked into my local Tesco to see a 'Inventory Checking' robot going about the store.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"Even more hilarious than it being called Tally is that nobody went within 5ft of it and kept giving it sideye."

Industry expert Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, revealed the trial after spotting the robot operating inside a Tesco store.

He said the move marks Tesco's first deployment of autonomous shelf-scanning technology and only the second time a major UK supermarket has trialled the system.

‌



"This marks a first for Tesco in the UK and only the second time we've seen a major UK retailer trialling autonomous shelf-scanning technology," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn.

"Rather than relying on manual audits, the robot captures shelf conditions multiple times a day and provides store teams with prioritised action lists via mobile apps and digital or printed reports.

"The goal is simple: resolve issues faster, improve inventory accuracy, and free up colleagues to spend more time serving customers."

‌



View 2 Images The Tally robot is being used at retailers in multiple other countries (Image: Jam Press/Simbe)

Tally, which was first introduced a decade ago, has already been used across retailers in several other countries.

Morrisons was the first UK supermarket to trial the machine last year, introducing it at stores in Wetherby, Redcar and Stockton.

‌



Those robots measured roughly 5ft4 inches in height and travelled across shop floors without assistance - using sensors to move around obstacles.

The new bots being used for the Tesco trial are reportedly 6.5ft tall.

During the Morrisons trial, the robot was used to check product placement and availability, and help ensure the correct pricing information was being displayed.

Article continues below

The supermarket introduced the technology to reduce the amount of time colleagues spent carrying out routine shelf inspections, allowing them to focus on assisting customers instead.

News.title: Cairngorms National Park wildfire sparks evacuations as residents told ‘leave pets’
News.content:
Cairngorms National Park wildfire sparks evacuations as residents told ‘leave pets’

Huge plumes of smoke have been coming from the Cairngorms National Park as a wildfire spreads in the Scottish Highlands

View 2 Images A large fire which is burning in the Cairngorms National Park (Image: Duncan Ferguson/PA Wire)

People have been evacuated from their homes due to a huge wildfire in the Highlands, with residents told "to leave your pets and go".

‌



Emergency services rushed to the scene after blaze broke out in the Cairngorms National Park on Wednesday afternoon - sending large volumes of smoke towards nearby towns.

‌



Four fire engines and specialist wildfire resources were scrambled to Ryvoan Bothy, near Nethy Bridge, with no reported injuries. It comes as wildfires have broken out up and down the country due to extreme heat, with the UK currently in its third heatwave of the year so far.

‌



Duncan Ferguson, from Glenmore near Aviemore, says police came to his house this afternoon telling residents to “leave your pets and go”.

View 2 Images People have been advised to keep their windows and doors closed (Image: Duncan Ferguson/PA Wire)

Ryanair issues airport delay warning to UK families over 15 destinations – list READ MORE :

He said the fire could become severe and affect property unless it was contained quickly. “It’s going to be bad, it’s going to be major unless they get hold of it. It’s heathland at the minute, but it’s started to burn in the upper area of the regeneration of the Caledonian pine forest," he stated.

‌



"Once it comes down into there, it’s dry, dry ground, with a real load to burn. It’s just going to get hotter and hotter.” Mr Ferguson, operations manager at the Spey Fishery Board, added that a nearby campsite had not yet been evacuated.

Glenmore Lodge, a nearby outdoors centre, said it was within the evacuation zone and advised travellers to avoid the area, reports Daily Record.

While the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) told residents in Aviemore, Glenmore and the surrounding communities to keep their doors and windows closed.

‌



Group commander Raymond King said: “We are currently in attendance at a large fire in the open near to Ryvoan Bothy within the Cairngorms National Park. Operations control were first alerted at 11.49am and we have mobilised four fire appliances and specialist wildfire resources to the area.

“There are no reported casualties. Due to large volumes of smoke travelling towards populated areas nearby, residents in Aviemore, Glenmore and the surrounding communities should keep their windows and doors closed.

“If you are within this area and can see or smell smoke, please follow the same advice. While we want people to enjoy the good weather, we ask that anyone in the Cairngorms National Park near to Aviemore and Glenmore avoid the area.

‌



“This part of the Cairngorms National Park is popular with hillwalkers, and we ask that people remain vigilant while active firefighting continues.”

A spokesperson for the Cairngorms National Park Authority said: “The ongoing incident near Ryvoan Bothy is deeply concerning, and we are grateful to all those who are working to tackle the fire. We would echo the advice of SFRS to avoid the area while firefighters and partners work to bring this blaze under control.

“This incident – alongside wildfires we are seeing across the UK this week – serves as a stark reminder of the risks that periods of drier, hotter weather can pose.”

‌



Firefighters are also battling a gorse fire at Garry Park Wood at Lochore Meadows Country Park in Fife. Videos seen on social media showed flames and smoke rising from the park.

The SFRS said they were alerted to the blaze at about 3.15pm on Wednesday, and mobilised one appliance to the scene. Parts of Scotland are at very high risk of wildfire over the next few days and the fire service has warned people to “stay vigilant” and act responsibly.

The SFRS, in conjunction with the Scottish Wildfire Forum, had earlier issued wildfire warnings for the central Highlands, southern and eastern Scotland. The alert, warning of a very high risk of wildfire, is in force from Wednesday until Monday.

Article continues below

It follows days of hot and dry weather in many parts of the country. The fire service said anyone who sees a large outdoor fire should call 999 immediately, giving the location and any other relevant information.

News.title: UK weather maps show new 36C heatwave surge with nine counties at 35C or more
News.content:
UK weather maps show new 36C heatwave surge with nine counties at 35C or more

Weather models show temperatures in the UK could soon surge back to 36C despite forecasts predicting that heatwave conditions will ease off from this weekend

View 3 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures soaring well above average later this month (Image: WXCHARTS)

Forecasters expect temperatures to cool off this weekend as the UK’s third heatwave of 2026 winds down, but weather models suggest it shouldn’t be too long before the mercury surges into the mid to high-30s once more.

‌



The Met Office expects peak temperatures to remain at 30C or 31C throughout this week until Saturday, before plunging significantly on Sunday when highs of 25C are forecast for southern areas and 22C in northern regions.

‌



Conditions will remain “dry and settled” into the weekend, the Met Office says, although with “cloud amounts generally increasing”. Despite temperatures “dropping towards the seasonal average”, the national weather agency expects conditions to still feel “pleasant in the sunshine”.

‌



View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 25 (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show heatwave ending in 6C chill as 27 counties plunge below 10C READ MORE :

The GFS weather model now suggests temperatures could surge back as high as 36C again on the following weekend. On July 25 (Saturday) it shows highs of 34C and 35C in western England, with 33C coming in Wales, 34C in the Midlands, and 34C in the south-east.

While on July 26 (Sunday) the data suggests highs of 36C are on the cards in the east of England. Temperatures could reach 34C/35C as far north as South Yorkshire, the maps show.

‌



Temperature anomaly maps for that weekend show the UK shaded in areas of orange and red. This indicates where temperatures are expected to rise well above the seasonal average.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 26 (Image: WXCHARTS)

In total, the GFS model maps show nine counties could see temperatures of 35C or above later this month. They are all in England.

Article continues below

UK counties facing 35C or more

Yorkshire

Nottinghamshire

Lincolnshire

Cambridgeshire

Norfolk

Suffolk

Herefordshire

Worcestershire

Gloucestershire

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office also expects temperatures to remain above average as we head towards the end of July. However, the national weather agency says there will be an increased chance of thunderstorms.

The Met Office forecast for July 19 to July 28 states: “Towards the latter part of July, the influence of high pressure may wane somewhat, allowing a greater chance of rain, showers or thunderstorms compared to earlier in the month. Overall, temperatures are expected to remain above average during this period.”

News.title: Teen sent chilling 'I've killed someone' text after hit-and-run, then ordered pizza
News.content:
Teen sent chilling 'I've killed someone' text after hit-and-run, then ordered pizza

Sonny Horsfall, 18, lost control of his car and slammed into an 84-year-old man before fleeing the scene and telling a friend 'I'm going to jail, I've killed someone'

View 3 Images Sonny Horsfall, 18, struck a pensioner and fled the scene (Image: Cleveland Police)

A teenager who ploughed his new car into an 84-year-old man texted a friend 'I've killed someone' after fleeing the scene.

‌



Sonny Horsfall, 18, lost control of his black Audi A4 on West Dyke Road in Redcar, North Yorkshire, on April 22.

‌



The vehicle flew over a patch of grass and hit a tree before slamming into the pensioner, who was walking along a footpath to get home at 10:23pm.

‌



Horsfall, who worked as a chef at a wellness retreat, ordered a pizza less than two hours after the crash - which saw the victim "thrown into the air," Durham Crown Court heard.

View 3 Images The case was heard at Durham Crown Court (Image: ncjMedia Ltd)

Elisha Marsay, prosecuting, told the court: "The front wheel of the Audi was hanging off; and there were orange sparks coming from the vehicle. The front windscreen was smashed and there was damage to the bonnet."

‌



An ambulance was called after a neighbour began screaming when she came across the victim lying on the grass, the court heard.

Horsfall, who was disqualified from driving, had already grabbed the car key and fled the scene by then, reports Teesside Live.

The court heard the teenager had purchased the Audi A4 from a friend, for £250, at 6pm that evening. By 11pm, he contacted the pal to say that he had "lost control" after coming out of a junction and had "hit someone".

‌



"I'm going to get seriously f***** for it," Horsfall messaged. "I went up the kerb. Bro, the man got smashed. He's bad, bro. I think I killed him."

The teenager had driven over 30 miles to Redcar that evening, and recorded Snapchat videos en route, the court heard.

On Skelton High Street, the video showed he was driving at 48mph over speed bumps. He wrote: "Smoke 'em boys" as he beeped at other drivers. "F*** the red lights," he typed, "you're getting dusted."

‌



After the crash, Horsfall messaged a pal on Snapchat saying: "Bro, I'm going to jail. I've killed someone. I hit someone in a car. Hit an old man, his head smashed the windscreen. My DNA all over the car. I smashed my face off the wheel. I ripped the key out and then I ran off."

He was arrested the following day after police found him in Malton.

View 3 Images The crash happened on West Dyke Road in Redcar (Image: Google)

‌



Horsefall, of Ryedale View in Kirkbymoorside, was today jailed for three years and disqualified from driving for four years.

The victim of the crash survived but suffered serious injuries which left him needing surgery to rebuild his hip. He was placed in an induced coma in hospital but has since made a good recovery, Ms Marsay said.

The pensioner said he did not remember the collision but suffered damage to his hip, broken bones in his back, and a broken foot.

‌



The crash also led to him being "largely immobile" after his operation and taking part in rehabilitation to learn how to walk again, he added. He can now walk a short distance using a walking frame. "I was a fit, healthy and independent 84-year-old man," the widower said.

"I was able to cook for myself, drive, and go out and meet people. The loss of my independence and dignity has been one of the hardest consequences of this incident. I really miss being able to get out and about as I used to."

The man said he does not know "what would have happened to me" if neighbours hadn't come out to help.

‌



Horsfall had earlier pleaded guilty to causing serious injury by dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified and with no insurance, and failing to stop after a road traffic accident.

His barrister Kelly Clarke told the court that "the man described in this offence, is in stark difference to the man I have met." Ms Clarke said that the 18-year-old is "suffering from PTSD and is not sleeping".

The defence barrister told the court that Horsfall said he'd taken "two pregabalin" tablets in the lead up to the crash and that he is now "wholly remorseful". "Custody has been a shock to him," Ms Clarke added. "He's been assaulted. Someone took a blade to his face and he required 16 stitches."

‌



Judge Christopher Knox told Horsfall that he had behaved "with wickedness and stupidity". He said that the friend who sold the Audi "made it clear that it was not in proper order".

"You lost control of the car, mounted the pavement and took out an active and law-abiding gentleman. He's suffered real injuries which are a disability to him," said the judge. "Because of his own force of character, and with the assistance of friends and family, he's made a remarkable recovery."

Investigating officer, Detective Constable Rachael Johnson, said: "This was a shocking and wholly avoidable collision which has left an 84-year-old man with serious injuries while simply walking home on the pavement."

Article continues below

Mr Johnson added: "It is hoped the sentence handed to Sonny Horsfall today serves as a clear reminder of the consequences of disregarding the rules of the road. Driving is a privilege and a responsibility, not a right.

"Anyone who gets behind the wheel without a licence, without insurance, or who drives recklessly is placing innocent members of the public at risk. The outcome of this case could easily have been fatal."

News.title: Man 'brutally punched seagull' in front of kids after it tried to steal his food
News.content:
Man 'brutally punched seagull' in front of kids after it tried to steal his food

Police are investigating after a man allegedly grabbed a seagull by the harbour in Porthleven, Cornwall and 'smashed' it against a wall because it tried to steal his food

View Image A seagull was allegedly attacked for trying to steal food (stock) (Image: Ian Cooper/North Wales Live)

Police are investigating after a man 'grabbed and punched' a seagull in front of traumatised children at a seaside town, allegedly leaving it with broken wings.

‌



Devon and Cornwall Police said the incident took place by the harbour in Porthleven, Cornwall on Monday afternoon, with an onlooker claiming the it happened because the bird tried to steal food.

‌



A witness on social media alleged the man attacked the seagull at the Harbour View Café when it attempted to take his food and he then "stuffed it through a fence" - where it was left with broken wings.

‌



"This man brutally and repeatedly smashed a seagull against the wall of the Harbour View Café because it tried to steal some food," said the person, who added that there were shocked children watching on.

Ryanair issues airport delay warning to UK families over 15 destinations – list READ MORE :

"He then stuffed the seagull through the fence onto the road, where it floundered with two broken wings. This was in front of numerous people and children who were hugely upset."

‌



Police are now appealing for anyone with relevant footage or information to come forward, reports CornwallLive.

A spokesperson for Devon and Cornwall Police said: "We have been made aware following a report of a seagull being injured by a man by the harbour in Porthleven on the afternoon of Monday, July 13.

"It was reported the suspect grabbed and punched the seagull leaving it injured. Enquiries into the matter are ongoing. Anybody with any relevant footage or information is asked to call 101 or visit our website quoting 50260183379."

Article continues below

Seagulls are protected by law as are all wild birds.

The RSPCA states on its website: "Like all wild birds, gulls, their chicks and their nests are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. This means it's illegal to intentionally kill, take or injure gulls, take or destroy their eggs, or damage or destroy any gull nests while they're in use or being built - unless you're acting under licence.

"Although gulls are a common sight in many areas near the coast, some species of gull, such as herring gulls and kittiwakes, are actually on the UK Red List. They're considered species of conservation concern in the UK because there's evidence suggesting that their populations are in decline overall."

News.title: Tom Kerridge shares Italian recipes and praises Andy Burnham's plans for hospitality
News.content:
Speaking ahead of the launch tonight of his new ITV show, Tom Kerridge Cooks Italy, top chef Tom Kerridge tells The Mirror: “When hospitality grows, the rest of the country grows. And Andy Burnham understands that.” It comes as Britain’s next Prime Minister calls for VAT in the sector to be slashed from 20% to 10%.

Owner with his wife, sculptor Beth Cullen-Kerridge, of The Hand and Flowers, near his home in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, it became the first and only pub to be awarded two coveted Michelin stars in 2006 and 2012. Tom, 52, who shares a son, Acey, 10, with Beth, says: “Hospitality needs to be backed and Andy Burnham is the man for the job.”

A lifelong Labour supporter, he adds: “I grew up in a single parent family on an estate in Gloucester. Labour represents a workforce, it tries to ensure that people have an opportunity regardless of background. If you come from a background that is economically struggling I think there should be systems in place: quality transport systems that allow you to get to work; a healthcare system that works.

View 9 Images Tom Kerridge is calling for VAT to be slashed from 20% to 10% "in line with the rest of Europe" (Image: Jam Press)

‌



“Irrespective if you grew up on an estate or a semi detached house, I think everyone should be presented with opportunities. The party that offers that has always been the Labour party.”

Burnham has proved himself in Manchester, says Tom, who ran popular eatery The Bull and Bear in the city from 2019 to 2022. He says: “Manchester is one of the most forward thinking, eclectic cities and that is something he has been a part of, keeping the cogs moving for reinvestment.

“Hospitality is at the base level of everything, exciting restaurants, great hotels, late night spaces. Manchester has all this energy that has been able to drive forward and allow investment and therefore other business to thrive too - property investment, tech companies, multimedia spaces.

“Manchester has a beating heart that comes from people hanging out together in hospitality. The rest of the country hasn't quite got that yet. What we want is the Andy Burnham approach.”

‌



View 9 Images When it comes to saving hospitality, Tom says: "Andy Burnham is the man for the job." (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Chef and publican Tom has spearheaded the #VATsTheProblem movement, gathering more than 250,000 signatures on a petition calling for a fairer 10% VAT rate for hospitality.

During his Makerfield campaign, Andy Burnham pledged to bring hospitality VAT down to 10%, to slash business rates for puns by 20% and to review cost pressures like National Insurance contributions. Tom says: “From my conversation with Andy I think he really understands.”

With industry sources saying one in six hospitality businesses are at risk of closure in the next year, Tom continues: “Things are shutting because of ongoing costs that have dropped in over many years of neglect of the industry: food inflation, energy bills, National Insurance increases.

‌



“On top of that, we have the second highest tax in Europe at 20%. Norway is 21%, everyone else is at between 8-12%. Ireland is dropping down to 9%. What we're asking for is to sit the same as Europe

View 9 Images Tom Kerridge and his wife, Beth Cullen-Kerridge (Image: Getty Images)

“We want growth, reinvestment, reemployment. If the Government could just get out of the way and let us operate, we are the beating heart of the reinvestment of the rest of the country.”

A familiar figure on our TV screens, Tom’s credits include Great British Menu, Saturday Kitchen, MasterChef, and he’s presented series including Tom Kerridge’s Proper Pub Food. And when he is not working, he is determined to use his fame to fight for the industry he loves.

‌



One nation that really knows how to do hospitality, according to Tom, is Italy, and he is great lover of Italian cuisine. Ahead of Tom Cooks Italy, he says: “Italian recipes are a celebration of ingredients and relatively simple. You don't need to be a super confident cook to try them or prepare for four days.

View 9 Images Tom says: "The Italian lifestyle is all based on food, restaurant, community, connection."

“I'm hooked on all things Italy after visiting. I've been back twice since we finished filming. I took the family to Pompeii then to see Napoli vs AC Milan, then to the Colosseum.”

Of Italians and their cuisine, he says: “They celebrate their produce, their culture, where it comes from - olive oil in Tuscany, for example. The lifestyle is all based on food, restaurant, community, connection. We should use Italy as an example of how we should do things.”

‌



And the passionate chef, who has shared a delicious Italian recipe with Mirror readers, remains optimistic about the future of British fare, too. He says: “Fingers crossed Andy Burnham brings in new energy. Andy Burnham is the man we need.”

*Tom Kerridge Cooks Italy, starts Thurs 16th July, 7.30pm on ITV1 and ITVX, proudly supported by M&S

Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew

View 9 Images Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew (Image: South Shore/ITV)

‌



Serves 4

2 tbsp olive oil

500g Italian style pork and fennel sausages

4 M&S Collection Master Grill Spicy Calabrian sausages, halved lengthways and sliced

2 onions, finely diced

4 cloves garlic, finely chopped

1 tsp fennel seeds

1 heaped tbsp tomato puree

2 Calabrian chillies, sliced

3 tbsp M&S Hot Calabrian chilli paste

200ml white wine

400ml chicken stock

4 sprigs fresh oregano, leaves picked

2 sprigs rosemary, finely chopped

2 cans chopped tomatoes

2 cans butterbeans, drained

2 tbsp flat leaf parsley, roughly chopped

For the garlic and chilli ciabatta

1 M&S ciabatta loaf

100g softened butter

1 tbsp M&S Hot Calabrian chilli paste

1 clove garlic, finely grated

‌



View 9 Images Calabrian chilli, sausage and butterbean stew (Image: Tom Regester/South Shore/ITV)

Method

Preheat oven to 180C fan Heat the oil in a large sauté pan. When hot, add the Italian style sausages and cook them until lightly browned on each side. Remove and place them onto a tray. Place the tray into the oven for 15-20 minutes. Next add the spicy Calabrian sausages to the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes. Add the onions to the pan and sautè for 5 minutes. Next add the garlic and stir gently for 2 more minutes. Add the fennel seeds and stir well. Pop in the tomato puree and chillies and stir again for another couple of minutes. Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half. Add in the stock and let that reduce by half. Add the tomatoes and bring up to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat, add the beans and herbs, cook for 15-20 minutes on low. Remove the sausages from the oven and let them rest for a few minutes. While the stew is cooking, mix the ingredients for the chilli butter together and season with a little salt. Halve the ciabatta lengthways and lay this onto a tray cut side up. Spread liberally with the chilli butter. Pop into the preheated oven and cook for 15 minutes or until golden and crunchy. Thickly slice the sausages and pop them into the stew. Finish with lots of fresh parsley and season with salt and pepper. Remove the bread from the oven and cut into thick pieces. Serve the sausage and butterbean stew into bowls with the chilli bread alongside.
